strand_a.summary: Clarifying and optimising civil, dual-use and defence research and innovation in future EU funding programmes. CLARIFYING AND OPTIMISING CIVIL, DUAL-USE AND DEFENCE R&I IN FUTURE EU FUNDING PROGRAMMES 3 Context This input note re-emphasises and builds on the key messages of the CESAER position of 30 April 2024, ‘Strengthen dual-use technologies by enhancing EU defence funding’, which remains unchanged: FP10 should continue to be a programme with a civil focus, allowing the framework programme to continue to set the global standard for supporting excellent research & innovation and cutting-edge science & technology. dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on European research and innovation funding. Separate primary evidence shows that a sudden security reclassification can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of European research and innovation funding.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for a sudden security reclassification.
Primary evidence contains 18 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on European research and innovation funding for current or planned work.
A sudden security reclassification reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: The primary corpus contains 5 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Avoid sudden funding gaps for capabilities that cannot pause without losing people or infrastructure.
Keep European and national funding routes coordinated when one programme is disrupted.
Use common, targeted screening rules rather than broad restrictions that fragment European access.
watch_for: Research previously treated as open is moved into a more restricted security category.
Different European countries apply materially different access decisions to the same work.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Well supported enough to watch closely, with contextual signals reinforcing rather than carrying the case.
